para.emphasis: A Technical and Legal Position Paper

section.title: Position
section.para: Transformer language models are graph databases in a technically precise, legally operative sense:

listitem.para: FFN layers are key-value stores — each layer encodes entity→relation→target triples addressable by vector similarity search, isomorphic to a property graph.
Forward passes are KNN graph walks — Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/√d_k)·V is KNN retrieval over the key-value graph.

LARQL demonstrates this directly — Chris Hay's open-source tool (github.com/chrishayuk/larql) extracts transformer weights into a queryable vindex and returns labelled edges via declarative LQL (DESCRIBE, WALK, INSERT INTO EDGES, COMPILE ... INTO MODEL FORMAT safetensors).

Memorisation is empirically confirmed — Llama 3.1 70B regenerates Harry Potter near-verbatim from a seed (Cooper et al. 2025); 100+ training images extracted from Stable Diffusion (Carlini et al. 2023).

Legal consequence — a model trained on protected works is a derivative work (17 U.S.C. § 101), a collective work, and a database subject to EU Directive 96/9/EC; distributing it distributes copies; GDPR Art. 17 erasure is technically feasible via INSERT INTO EDGES.

section.title: Build
section.para: This paper is validated and built to HTML by the same uniform pipeline as every other document in the corpus -- see .github/workflows/build-corpus.yml (real DocBook 5.2 RELAX NG via jing, this project's DCTERMS completeness policy check, then xsltproc against the official docbook-xsl-ns xhtml5 stylesheet, writing src/01-llm-database-theory.html next to its source, same as any other document). There is nothing paper-specific to validate or build to HTML; running the corpus pipeline against src/*.xml manually reproduces it locally.
This directory's own Makefile only covers the one thing that genuinely is unique to this document: LaTeX/PDF output.

section.title: FOF-AI-1
section.para: The FFN layers of a transformer LLM function as key-value stores structurally isomorphic to a property graph.
Evidence: LARQL demonstration; Self-Attention as Parametric Endofunctor (arXiv:2501.02931)

section.title: FOF-AI-2
section.para: LARQL returns labelled directed edges from transformer weights via declarative LQL queries, without retraining or structural modification.

section.title: FOF-AI-3
section.para: Llama 3.1 70B regenerates the first Harry Potter novel near-verbatim from a seed of the opening tokens.
Evidence: Cooper et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.12546) — "copied inside the model parameters"

section.title: FOF-AI-4
section.para: Over 100 near-identical training images, including trademarked logos, were extracted from Stable Diffusion and Imagen.

section.title: FOF-AI-5
section.para: A measurable fraction of diffusion-model outputs are near-exact copies of training images.

section.title: FOF-AI-6
section.para: OpenAI and Google stated to the U.S. Copyright Office that their models store no copies of training data — only numbers.
Evidence: Admissions compilation (arXiv:2603.20957) — contradicted by FOF-AI-3 through FOF-AI-5.

row.entry: An LLM trained on protected works is a derivative work under 17 U.S.C. § 101
An LLM trained on multiple copyrighted works is a collective work under 17 U.S.C. § 101
A deployed LLM qualifies as a database under EU Directive 96/9/EC (sui generis right)
GDPR Art. 17 right to erasure is technically feasible via INSERT INTO EDGES
The format defence ("only numbers") fails the 17 U.S.C. § 101 machine-perceptibility test
FOF-AI-2 through FOF-AI-5; Litchfield v. Spielberg 736 F.2d 1352
Distribution and API access to an LLM are database acts requiring rights-holder authorisation

section.title: Connections to Legal-Theory Corpus
section.para: This paper strengthens and unifies arguments across three existing matters:

listitem.para: copyright-ip-authorship — FOF-AI-1 through FOF-AI-6 are ready for incorporation into the findings stub; provides the derivative-work and collective-work technical predicates.
platform-tos-constitutional-limits — resolves the data-vs-program ambiguity in llm-data-vs-program.xml; informs the database-retrieval-vs-speech First Amendment analysis.

agpl-ai-training-and-code-licensing — provides the technical premise for the GPL derivative-works / poison-pill argument: training on GPL code encodes GPL-licensed edges into the vindex, retrievable by LARQL.

section.para: See src/02-legal-corpus-connections.xml for the full analysis.

section.title: Open Questions
section.para: These are working notes, not a citable claim of this article -- see scratch/notes.md for the detailed list this summarizes (session provenance, per-source verification tiers, and the full gap inventory). That file, and its companion scratch/formulas.md, are retained as real, deliberate cross-references to supplementary material that lives outside this paper's formal citable body (src/*.xml) rather than folded into it or silently dropped: they are dated research-session artifacts (deep-research workflow output, confidence tiers, math derivations) useful for provenance and follow-on work, not polished, citation-ready prose fit for the article itself. Key gaps:

listitem.para: Source attribution precision — LARQL returns semantic triples; it does not yet identify which training document is the source of a specific edge. Needed for litigation standing.
GDPR erasure at person-level — feasibility of identifying and removing edges for a specific named individual without corrupting surrounding graph structure.
EU Database Directive case law — no ECJ ruling yet on whether AI weights qualify; watch for national court referrals.
